absent: Full layouts of vmap area, virtual-memory descriptor and per-node structures plus allocation-side locking.
Semantics of page-table helpers, TLB and cache flushes, lazy MMU mode and architecture sync mask.
Generic I/O remap mapping implementation, protection handling and ownership test.
Complete daemon lifecycle, registration, main loop timing and collapse execution beyond the isolate prologue.
Full slot object layout, hash table definition and reference-count rules.
Tracepoint payloads and virtual-memory event counters for collapse outcomes.
Sanitizer, debug allocation, file-cache and charge interactions around unmap and collapse.

findings.text: Removal of a virtual mapping validates page alignment and ability to sleep, unlinks the area for the address, returns null when absent or has no descriptor, otherwise runs debug and sanitizer checks, tears down mappings and frees the area while returning the descriptor.
Unmap entry tolerates a null address, forbids interrupt context and may sleep, delegates to removal, warns when no area exists, then releases the descriptor; the no-MMU variant always faults.

Kernel range teardown requires a forward range, walks top-level table chunks, skips empty or bad entries, descends into populated subtrees, accumulates a modification mask and requests architecture synchronization when the mask intersects the architecture mask.

Middle page-table levels clear huge entries before descending, record huge or bad state in the mask, skip empty or bad entries, warn when a cleared huge span is shorter than the level size, and at the PMD level cooperatively reschedule while iterating.

Leaf teardown runs under lazy MMU mode, advances by one base page or by a larger hugetlb unmap size when applicable, realigns address and pointer on misalignment, clears through the initial address space and marks leaf modification, warning on entries that are neither empty nor present.
Area release flushes cache for the span, unmaps without flushing, conditionally flushes kernel TLB range when debug page allocation is active, then frees the area object without flushing.
Lookup and unlink starts at the node derived from the address and cycles over all nodes, holding each node busy spinlock only across find plus unlink, returning the first hit and otherwise null.

I/O mapping with protection delegates to a generic helper; generic unmap aligns the address down to a page boundary and unmaps only when the address belongs to the I/O remap region; public unmap delegates to the generic helper.

Collapse control carries an origin flag distinguishing daemon from direct requests, per-node scan counters, a progress counter, a nodemask for allocation fallback, and a bitmap sized to table fanout recording occupied slots.
Daemon scan cursor carries a list head of candidate address spaces, a pointer to the current slot, and a current address; the global instance starts with an empty list.
Address-space slot access hashes by the address-space pointer and selects the entry with pointer equality, returning null when absent; removal detaches the entry from both hash and list.
Maximum tolerated empty, swapped or shared entries is one less than the huge-page fanout; slot hash uses ten bits; smallest multi-size collapse order is two.

Daemon tunables default scan sleep to ten seconds and allocation sleep to sixty seconds, with read-mostly controls for pages per scan and per-class maxima plus counters for collapsed pages and full scans and an expiry timestamp.
A sysfs group named for the daemon exposes nine attributes covering defrag mode, three per-class maxima, pages to scan, two read-only counters, and two sleep intervals.

Sysfs stores parse base-ten integers and reject parse failures; pages per scan must be nonzero, per-class maxima must not exceed fanout minus one, and sleep stores reset the expiry and wake the daemon.

Empty-entry tolerance is zero when userfaultfd is armed and unrestricted for direct collapse; PMD order honors the tunable while multi-size orders scale the maximum when the tunable is at its limit and otherwise use zero with a one-time warning for intermediate tunables.
Shared and swapped tolerance is unrestricted for direct collapse, forbidden for multi-size collapse, and tunable-honoring for PMD collapse.
Huge-page advice toggles per-area flags: huge advice clears the opt-out flag and sets the opt-in flag, while no-huge advice does the reverse and thereby excludes the area from daemon scanning.

Address-space exit holds a dedicated spinlock across slot lookup and removal unless the slot is the active scan cursor; freeing outside the lock clears the huge flag, releases the cache object and drops a reference, while the active-slot path serializes with write-mode address-space locking.
Daemon control uses a dedicated mutex and slot hash plus expiry use a dedicated spinlock; the thread pointer and tunables are mostly read-only after setup.

Isolation scan walks one leaf entry per base page, counts empty-or-zero and shared entries against maxima, and aborts with distinct codes for over-limit, non-present, userfaultfd, abnormal or device pages, lazyfree without droppable allowance, preexisting large mappings, and lock contention.

Emptiness means missing or present zero page; referenced means folio youth or leaf youth or notifier youth; event accounting updates the PMD counter plus an order-specific statistic; scan initialization clears node loads, allocation mask and presence bitmap.

Failure unwind walks scanned leaves backward releasing small present non-zero folios then drains the compound list, adjusting isolated anon or file accounting, unlocking and returning each folio to reclaim.

Removal and unmap may sleep and must not run in interrupt context, warning on misaligned or unknown addresses; the page-table walk asserts forward progress and warns on truncated huge spans or unexpected leaf states.
Collapse eligibility test reports disabled when the address space is exiting or has fully disabled transparent huge pages.

Scan outcome enumeration distinguishes success from many aborts covering missing tables, mapped huge pages, quota overruns, page and VMA state, allocation and charge failure, truncation, and copy or writeback problems.
